message_1_subject: MAP: Closebench perf targets & test windows
message_1_body:
Jordan — attaching the updated MAP and the perf test plan we discussed. TL;DR and asks below.

Summary (MAP items):
- Objective: Validate production latency/throughput & TTFT for your peak workflow; demonstrate stable behavior under burst vs steady-state.
- Target SLAs for close: p95 latency <= 2.0s for interactive path, TTFT p50 < 0.8s, sustained throughput >= 300 rps for 30m.
- Concurrency scenarios: burst probes (10k rps 60s), ramp-to-steady (gradual increase to 300 rps), long steady-state (30 min), and queueing backpressure sweep.
- Acceptance criteria: no >1% error rate, queue depth <= 80 per worker, graceful throttling (429s) with explicit retry guidance.

Please confirm test windows you can commit to next week (we suggested Thu 10/15 AM PT or Sat 10/17 early window). Also confirm whether SOC2 evidence must be included in the MAP deliverables.

Attachments: MAP_Closebench_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones), perf-test-plan.md (detailed test script).

Next steps for Redwood: Rishi will own test orchestration & results writeup; Karthik will validate rate-limit tuning and fallback policies. I'll update the HubSpot MAP and push a DocuSign SOW once tests pass acceptance.

Thanks,
Naomi

message_3_subject: Re: MAP: Closebench perf targets & test windows — test design details
message_3_body:
Jordan — good questions, high-level answers and test design below. Long version attached (burst-playback-results.csv + inline plan):

1) TTFT definition: our TTFT numbers in the MAP are E2E when measured from the client load generator to the SDK edge and back (includes network); we will run the generator from an AWS us-west-2 instance you provide or from our dedicated test runner in the same region.

2) Burst intent & handling: the 10k rps burst is a stress probe to exercise autoscaling, cache behavior, and graceful fallbacks. It's not expected as a steady production pattern; acceptance does not require surviving an unbounded burst without throttling. Expected behavior during burst:
  - Immediate autoscale cannot provision infinite GPU capacity; we expect short-duration queueing + 429s when queue thresholds exceeded.
  - Success criteria: no more than 3% of requests fail with 5xx; client receives clear 429 with Retry-After header; overall degradation should be graceful with latency corridors (p50/p95 increase but p99 < 5s).

3) Concrete test matrix (we will run these sequentially in the agreed window):
  A) Ramp probe: 0 -> 300 rps over 5 minutes, hold 300 rps for 30 minutes (steady-state). Collect TTFT, p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and queue depth per worker.
  B) Burst playback: three bursts at 10k rps for 60s, separated by 5 minutes of warmup. Measure failure patterns and scaling events.
  C) Queueing sweep: iterate target concurrency points (50, 100, 200, 400) and measure queue depth, queue latency, and throttling triggers.

4) Expected baseline numbers (reference model: rw-instruct-7B quantized Q4):
  - TTFT (E2E client-measured): p50 ~0.65s, p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.6s at steady 300 rps with batching and KV cache hit rate ~70%.
  - Throughput: ~320 tokens/s per GPU host in current config; observed sustained request throughput ~340 rps per pool shard.
  - Queue thresholds: we tune per-host queue target to 120 concurrent requests to avoid head-of-line latency spikes.

5) Rate-limit tuning & fallback policy recommendations (we will apply these during the run):
  - Client-side: soft rate window around 90% of target rps, exponential backoff on 429 with jitter.
  - Server-side: immediate request admission up to queue depth 120, then fast-fail with 429 + Retry-After. Canary fallback to smaller quantized model under sustained elevated latency.

I'll coordinate the exact test runner IPs and the measurement scripts. We'll upload raw CSVs and a summarized MAP entry after the run.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
